title: Add release team for niwcpac
author: xydesa
body:

* Release repositories to add:
  * [rqt_dotgraph](https://github.com/niwcpac/rqt_dotgraph)

comments.author: denewiler
comments.body:
I have a rosdistro branch ready to go that adds a new package to rosdistro distribution.yaml files if we need to do that first.

https://github.com/ros/rosdistro/compare/master...tdenewiler:rosdistro:rqt-dotgraph

comments.author: nuclearsandwich
comments.body:
@denewiler @xydesa before the release team is created, the PR to rosdistro which adds the `source` (and optionally `doc`) entries should be created so that the package can undergo license and naming review. The `release` stanza should be omitted from the manually created PR and added by using the `bloom` utility to create the release once the release repository is created.

Once the linked comparison has been opened as a PR and merged into ros/rosdistro please update this request.

comments.author: xydesa
comments.body: @nuclearsandwich Thanks for letting us know. FYI the [ROS2 documentation](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/How-To-Guides/Releasing/First-Time-Release.html) makes it seem like we needed a release team first and the ticket template in here is ambiguous on that count. Which is why I made this PR first.

comments.author: nuclearsandwich
comments.body:
> FYI the [ROS2 documentation](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/How-To-Guides/Releasing/First-Time-Release.html) makes it seem like we needed a release team first and the ticket template in here is ambiguous on that count. Which is why I made this PR first.

It's a bit labyrinthine but the documentation for [Creating a release repository](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/How-To-Guides/Releasing/Release-Team-Repository.html#create-a-new-release-repository) points out that "If your repository is new to the ROS community, you should first open a pull request on [ros/rosdistro](https://github.com/ros/rosdistro) adding a source entry for your repository."

Building better tooling for this workflow (or optimizing it away) is definitely in my goals for the future.
